findings.claim: The test pins the incidental current size of package-lock.json (`assert.equal(lstatSync(...).size, 568_011)`) instead of the invariant it means to assert (size < PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_PACKAGE_LOCK_MAX_BYTES), so any ordinary dependency change fails the shadow suite with an unrelated equality error, and the hardcoded 568,011 in docs/ops/prompt-refiner-shadow-harness.md section 2 and docs/ops/tomverse-chat-progress.md goes stale at the same moment; the follow-on `assert.ok(568_011 < CAP)` compares two literals and can never fail.
findings.reproduction: Add or bump any dependency (e.g. `npm install --save-dev <pkg>` so package-lock.json changes length), then `npm run test:prompt-refiner-shadow`. The case fails at the first assertion with `Expected values to be strictly equal: <new size> !== 568011` while the 4 MiB cap logic and every other assertion in the case still hold. Replacing the two assertions with `const size = lstatSync(...).size; assert.ok(size < PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_PACKAGE_LOCK_MAX_BYTES);` keeps the intended check and removes the doc coupling.

findings.claim: These four patterns have no leading slash, so Git matches them at every directory depth and they pin files outside the harness allowlist, contradicting the block comment's claim that this is a "narrow list" that keeps "line-ending policy for the rest of the repository" unchanged (apps/mobile/package.json, packages/chat-core/package.json, packages/ui-tokens/package.json, apps/mobile/tsconfig.json and packages/chat-core/tsconfig.json are now `text eol=lf` too).
findings.reproduction: `git check-attr text eol -- apps/mobile/package.json packages/chat-core/tsconfig.json` at this commit prints `text: set` and `eol: lf` for both, although only the repo-root package.json and tsconfig.json appear in PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_SOURCE_PATHS (lib/promptRefinerShadowSource.ts:11-25). Anchoring the four entries as `/.gitattributes`, `/package.json`, `/package-lock.json`, `/tsconfig.json` makes the attribute scope equal the allowlist; the harness's byte comparison is unaffected either way because a mismatched checkout already fails closed with `runtime_source_drift`.

verdict.nextAction: Both round-1 nits are closed (dedicated 4 MiB lockfile cap with a `cat-file -s` pre-check under an 8 MiB bounded capture, and the node_modules/installation-provenance limit now stated in AGENTS.md, the ops doc section 2 and the policy doc section 9); proceed to Linux integration CI, optionally folding the two nits above into a follow-up.
